text:
anna: quick q — if we go active/active, how do we handle PII tenant residency for shadow writes? legal flagged it as risky.
marc: +1. don't auto-shadow PII tenants. we should require an explicit consent or escrow token before replicating writes.
sophie: what about a per-tenant config: `residency_mode: {local_only, async_replica_with_consent, blocked}`. default = local_only for PII scopes.
raj: ops note — async_replica_with_consent still adds background workload. need to measure tail QPS impact and KV cache churn.
anna: good point. do we want the control plane to enforce `blocked` at routing level (deny request to other regions) vs returning 403 from datalayer?
marc: I'd enforce at proxy/router level (cheaper, prevents cross-region serialization). routing decision tree should short-circuit before touching backend.
sophie: agreed. also need a header to carry consent token: `X-Redwood-PII-Consent: <token>` and a short TTL so tokens can't be reused indefinitely.
raj: can we use the existing escrow DB? reusing it avoids new secrets surface but may inflate read pressure. propose caching consent tokens at edge for 30s.
anna: sounds reasonable. follow-ups: (1) define router enforcement API, (2) add proxy cache for consent tokens, (3) update docs and legal checklist.
deploy-bot: deploy/patch-4712 finished on infra-staging — added header passthrough and a feature-flag `residency_proxy_enforce` :thumbsup:
